title: Discovery of new polyacetylenes from the rhizomes of  Adenia cardiophylla  through activity-directed phytochemical investigation and evaluation of their anti-inflammatory properties
content: Adenia cardiophylla (Mast.) Engl. Passifloraceae has long been used in traditional medicine throughout Vietnam and Southeast Asia for the treatment of rheumatism, bone pain, and pneumonia. Based on bioassay-guided isolation, seven previously undescribed compounds, including one cyanogenic glycoside (1), four polyacetylenes (2–4, 6), and two cyclopentene carboxylic acid derivatives (20 and 21), together with sixteen known compounds from the rhizomes of Adenia cardiophylla were isolated. The chemical structures were determined by detailed spectroscopic methods (UV, IR, HRMS, NMR), ECD, and computational NMR calculation methods. Anti-inflammatory activity was evaluated by measuring nitric oxide (NO) production in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophage cells. Notably, the n-hexane and ethyl acetate extracts significantly inhibited NO production with IC50 values of 43.53 ± 1.91 and 31.43 ± 2.32 µg mL−1, respectively. Compounds 2–5, 7, and 8 remarkably suppressed NO production with IC50 values of 47.29 ± 1.09, 47.16 ± 2.01, 31.43 ± 0.73, 18.35 ± 0.87, 48.04 ± 0.69, and 40.67 ± 4.36 µM, respectively. Furthermore, the new cyanogenic glycoside (1) slightly inhibited cell proliferation in A549 cancer cells (IC50 = 44.51 ± 0.24 µM). Compound 5 displayed modulation of the TLR4/IKKβ/NF-κB signaling pathway with suppression of downstream inflammatory mediators, including iNOS, COX-2, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, via in silico study. These findings suggested that polyacetylene derivatives (2–8) may represent the principal constituents involved in preventing the progression of inflammation, thereby providing scientific evidence to support their therapeutic potential.
